items.title: Samsung Announces December Release for Intelligent Eyewear, Bringing a Smarter Way To See the World
items.excerpt: Combining Samsung engineering with 30 unique designs from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker,
items.rationale: Primary-source launch of the Gemini-powered Android XR glasses (30 Gentle Monster/Warby Parker frames, $395/$449, Dec 10 release in US/Korea); the single eyewear card the run allows.

items.title: Windows 11 Photos is getting Adobe's generative AI tools in December
items.excerpt: Adobe and Microsoft are bringing generative AI image editing and Adobe Express integration to Windows 11 Photos, with a preview scheduled for Windows Insiders in December 2026. The partnership also introduces performance optimizations for Adobe products on Nvidia RTX Spark-powered Windows PCs.
items.rationale: Adobe generative editing lands inside the default Windows photo app (Insider preview in December), so a built-in OS tool now gets Adobe-grade AI edits.

items.title: MSI’s Compact AI Desktop Packs Up to 128GB of Unified Memory | MSI EdgeMesa N AI
items.excerpt: MSI’s EdgeMesa N AI+ pairs up to 128GB of unified memory with NVIDIA Blackwell graphics in a compact desktop built for local AI development.
items.rationale: New MSI product launch: a compact desktop built for running and developing AI models locally (up to 128GB unified memory, Nvidia Blackwell), so AI is the device's purpose, not a side feature.

items.title: Anker’s tiny AI recorder gets voice dictation support with Typeless
items.excerpt: Typeless, the AI-powered voice dictation and text-processing app, has just announced an official partnership with Anker to bring its AI voice dictation app to the Soundcore Work wearable microphone. The tiny recorder isn’t exactly new, though. Anker introduced it at CES 2026, and it has been on sale for quite some time. The latest integration […]
items.rationale: New partnership turns an existing wearable AI recorder into a dictation input: Typeless voice-to-text now runs through the Soundcore Work mic.

items.title: Apple Says HomeView Software Update Coming Next Month With Siri Fix
items.excerpt: In her HomeView review shared in a free edition of her New Things newsletter today, tech journalist Joanna Stern said Siri AI once told her "I don't have a camera to see you," even though the device has a camera. Apple confirmed to Stern that it plans to release a software update in December with a fix for this issue. Siri AI also refused to open Stern's garage door or unlock her front door, even
items.rationale: Apple confirms a December HomeView update to fix Siri AI failures found in the first reviews, a concrete new commitment beyond the October launch coverage.

https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-.new_action: Official launch announcement on 11-12: full 30-frame lineup (16 Gentle Monster, 14 Warby Parker), pricing ($395/$449) and a firm Dec 10 US/Korea release date. The 11-06 card only reported that pre-orders would open.

https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/app.new_action: Apple confirmed a December HomeView software update that fixes Siri AI failures (camera denial, refusing door and garage commands). This is a new vendor commitment, not more launch coverage. The tagged match 9to5mac 2026-10-18 (next-gen HomeView rumor) is a different story.
